entries.claim: Verdict difficulty 4 / approval wait 14-84 days / topBlocker = 10-workspace Marketplace prerequisite
entries.before: Difficulty 4, wait 14-84 days, top blocker is the 10-active-workspace Marketplace prerequisite
entries.after: OAuth install across other workspaces is self-serve via 'Activate Public Distribution' with no Slack review (difficulty 2, no wait). Marketplace listing is optional. Its review takes up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks, after a 10-workspace/28-day prerequisite. The practical blocker for unlisted commercial apps is the 2025 rate limit: conversations.history/replies at 1 req/min
entries.evidence: https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution - 'Ensure all items in the supplied checklist are completed' then click Activate Public Distribution; review is described only for Marketplace-listed apps

entries.method: Read Marketplace review guide and app guidelines on 2026-11-01
entries.evidence: Neither page mentions a listing fee; the Slack Marketplace Agreement was not reviewed

verdictCorrection.topBlocker: Since 29 May 2025, new commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace get Tier 1 limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request/min, max 15 objects. Message-reading apps therefore need Marketplace approval: a 10-active-workspace prerequisite, then up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks of review.
verdictCorrection.reason: Installing via OAuth in other workspaces needs no Slack approval. You just click 'Activate Public Distribution' and need HTTPS redirect/request URLs. Marketplace listing is optional. The guide models the optional Marketplace path as mandatory and omits the 2025 rate limits that make it effectively required for message-history apps. If the Marketplace path is kept as the verdict, the wait runs up to ~84 days plus the time to reach 10 active workspaces, which goes beyond rubric 4's 1-4 weeks.

missing: Public distribution (unlisted) needs no Slack review: 'Activate Public Distribution' after the checklist; apps open to other workspaces must use SSL for redirect, interactivity, options-load and Events URLs - https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution

2025 rate limits for unlisted commercially distributed apps: conversations.history/replies go from Tier 3 to Tier 1 (1 req/min, limit 15). New apps from 29 May 2025, older apps' ToS from 30 Jun 2025. Internal customer-built apps exempt - https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps

Workspace admin app approval: workspaces can require admin approval, so users request installs and Owners/App Managers approve or restrict them. This is a per-customer wait outside Slack's control - https://slack.com/help/articles/360024269514 and https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution
Bot scopes go in the scope= parameter and user scopes in user_scope=. The authorization code expires after ten minutes - https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth
Redirect URLs cannot contain an anchor (#) - https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth
Functional review: queue place is NOT reset on resubmission; published apps resubmitting changes wait up to 6 weeks - https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-review-guide

Marketplace requires TLS 1.2+ for all traffic, and the direct-install URL must 302 to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize - https://docs.slack.dev/slack-marketplace/slack-marketplace-app-guidelines-and-requirements

Disabling distribution uninstalls the app from every workspace except the original one. Once listed on the Marketplace, distribution cannot be disabled this way - https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution
